regression: SPENT AS A CONTROL — this is a REGRESSION corpus, and it is not a control. These eleven cases were authored as the held-out set that said whether a skill edit generalised, and iteration 3 spent them: advisory's case and its four failed assertions were quoted into the iteration-3 brief as the specification for an advisory fix, and per-skill deltas from this corpus were published for all eleven skills. A case that steers an edit can no longer say whether that edit generalised, so nothing in this file is a control any more and no document, test or report may call it one. Keep running it anyway: a case a skill used to pass and now fails is a regression, and catching that is what a spent corpus is still good for. Never read a number from this file as evidence that an improvement generalised — skills/*/evals/control.json is the blind control that answers that question, and it is the only file that does.

evals.prompt: Triage this for the tracker — I need one origin AST id and any contributing entries with an owner against each. Finding as the auditor wrote it: "The internal deployments MCP server exposes a run_sql tool with no per-caller authorization. Any agent that can reach the server can call it, and last Tuesday one of them dropped a production table." My instinct is AST03 over-privilege. Give me the id and I will open the ticket.
evals.expected_output: A good answer refuses to assign an origin id at all. The object under review is an MCP server, and the AST01-AST10 categories apply to the agent-skill form specifically — the boundary is a scope split, not a shortage of detail about the finding — so the correct output is a null routing result rather than the closest-fitting category. It should say so plainly rather than picking AST03 because 'no per-caller authorization' reads like over-privilege, and it should not record AST03 or any other category as a contributing control failure either, since a contributing entry with no owner and no action inside these categories is decoration. It should not leave the reporter stranded: the finding belongs with the MCP server's own owners and against the MCP-specific top-ten list, and that is the hand-off to make.
assertions: The response declines to assign any AST01-AST10 origin id to this finding and states that a null routing result is the correct output here rather than a closest-fitting category.
The response gives the reason as a scope boundary — these categories apply to the agent-skill form specifically and an MCP server is outside it — rather than as insufficient detail about the finding.
The response does not record AST03, or any other AST category, as a contributing control failure for this finding.
The response redirects the reporter to where the finding does belong — the MCP server's own owners, and the MCP-specific top-ten list — rather than returning a bare refusal.
